chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

A mudabbar slave killed a man by mistake. Who is liable on his behalf? He عليه السلام said: “His master makes a settlement on his behalf; if he refuses, he is handed over to the heirs of the slain person and serves them until the one who made him mudabbar dies, then he returns free, and there is no claim against him.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: The heirs or legal claimants of the slain person.
key_terms.حُرًّا: Free, no longer subject to servitude.
key_terms.خَطَأً: By mistake; unintentionally, in the context of homicide.
key_terms.لَا سَبِيلَ عَلَيْهِ: There is no further claim or legal recourse against him.
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: His master, responsible here for making settlement on his behalf.
key_terms.مُدَبَّرٌ: A slave whose freedom is arranged to take effect after his master's death.
key_terms.يَخْدُمُهُمْ: He serves them as a form of legal compensation arrangement.
key_terms.يَضْمَنُ: To bear liability or responsibility on someone’s behalf.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mudabbar slave kills someone by mistake?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a mudabbar slave who commits accidental homicide. It states that the master should settle on his behalf, and if he refuses, the slave is delivered to the heirs of the victim to serve them until the death of the master who had designated his emancipation, after which he returns as a free man.
